The '''2011–12 Serie A''' (known as the [[Serie A]] [[Telecom Italia Mobile|TIM]] after its headline sponsors) was the 110th season of top-tier Italian [[association football|football]], the 80th in a [[round-robin tournament]], and the second since its organization under a league committee separate from [[Serie B]]. It began on 3 September 2011 and ended on 13 May 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.legaseriea.it/it/sala-stampa/archivio-dettaglio/-/news/DATE_STAGIONE_SPORTIVA_2011_2012/430992|title=Date stagione sportiva 2011-2012|date=23 June 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110730083654/http://www.legaseriea.it/it/sala-stampa/archivio-dettaglio/-/news/DATE_STAGIONE_SPORTIVA_2011_2012/430992 |archive-date=30 July 2011 |website=Lega Serie A|language=it}}</ref> The league was originally scheduled to start on 27 August, but this was delayed due to a strike by the players.<ref>{{cite news|title=Italian players' strike delays start of Serie A season|publisher=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14672599|access-date=25 September 2011}}</ref> The fixtures were drawn up on 27 July 2011.

The league title was won by [[Juventus FC|Juventus]], winning its 28th official Serie A title or ''[[scudetto]]'', and first since the [[2005–06 Serie A]]. The team completed the season undefeated, becoming the first team to do so in a 38-game league season in Italy; [[A.C. Perugia Calcio|Perugia]] were undefeated in the 30-game [[1978–79 Serie A]], in which they finished second in the table, while [[A.C. Milan|Milan]] were unbeaten and won the title in the 34-game [[1991–92 Serie A]].<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.goal.com/en-us/news/86/italy/2012/05/13/3100053/juventus-completes-the-serie-a-season-unbeaten-following#| title = Juventus completes the Serie A season unbeaten following home win over Atalanta {{!}} Goal.com}}</ref>

Since Italy dropped from third to fourth place in the [[UEFA association coefficient rankings]] at the end of the 2010–11 season,<ref>{{cite web|title=UEFA Country Ranking 2011|url=http://www.xs4all.nl/~kassiesa/bert/uefa/data/method4/crank2011.html|publisher=Bert Kassies|access-date=14 April 2011}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2011-02-25 |title=Italy to lose Euro spot |url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/serie-a/2009-2010/italy-to-lose-euro-spot_sto2681850/story.shtml |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250120112408/https://www.eurosport.com/football/serie-a/2009-2010/italy-to-lose-euro-spot_sto2681850/story.shtml |url-status=dead |archive-date=20 January 2025 |access-date=2023-06-05 |website=Eurosport |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Honigstein |first=Raphael |date=2011-03-02 |title=Raphael Honigstein: Differing mindsets have Germany, Italy going in opposite directions |url=https://www.si.com/more-sports/2011/03/02/bundesliga-serie |access-date=2023-06-05 |website=Sports Illustrated |language=en-us}}</ref> the league lost a group stage berth for the [[UEFA Champions League]] from the 2012–13 season.

==Rule changes==
The rules for the registration of non-EU (or non-[[EFTA]] or Swiss) nationals transferred from abroad were revised in the summer of 2011. Clubs could now sign two non-EU players. This was a reverse of the decision made the previous summer in the wake of [[Italy national football team|Italy]]'s failure at the [[2010 FIFA World Cup|2010 World Cup]] that limited clubs to the signing of just one such player.{{Citation needed|date=September 2011}}

===Managerial changes===
In Italy, football managers are only permitted to manage one club per season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://forzaitalianfootball.com/2011/06/what-if-the-one-club-per-season-rule-was-scrapped/|title=What If... the 'One Club per Season' Rule Was Scrapped?|date=7 June 2011}}</ref> For this purpose, the "season" is defined as starting when its first match kicks off, so [[Roberto Donadoni]] and [[Stefano Pioli]], who lost their job at [[Cagliari Calcio|Cagliari]] and [[U.S. Città di Palermo|Palermo]] on 12 and 31 August 2011 were able to take respectively the [[Parma Calcio 1913|Parma]] job in January 2012 and the [[Bologna F.C. 1909|Bologna]] job in October 2011 because the first matches were not until 9 September 2011.

==Awards==
The Gran Galà del Calcio AIC 2012 was the second edition of the awards ceremony organized by the [[Italian Footballers' Association]] (AIC), recognizing the best performers of the 2011–12 Serie A. The awards were presented on 27 January 2013 at the Teatro Dal Verme in Milan.
